note: Deterministic input -> output cases. No model is involved. Every case is either arithmetic that must reproduce to the paisa, or a case the engine must REFUSE. Add cases here rather than in Python. All figures are synthetic or rounded beyond identification.

cases.source: [documented] The proviso to s.139(8A) bars an updated return that results in a refund or increases one. [observed] The guard read the section only as an exclusion, so an explicit --filing-section 139(8A) with an in-window date walked past it and printed a refund at exit 0. The section a filer states is direct evidence; the date is the fallback inference.
[observed] The same guard was date-driven, so an explicit 139(8A) with NO date at all also slipped it. A stated section needs no date to be believed.
[documented] s.139(5) is a revised return, not an updated one, and may carry a refund. The guard must not over-refuse now that it reads the section directly.

s.44ADA presumes 50% of gross receipts as profit; ceiling 50 lakh, or 75 lakh where cash receipts are 5% or less — references/forms-itr1-itr3-itr4.md, Presumptive rates and ceilings

the same receipts are within the scheme once cash receipts are stated to be 5% or less
declaring below 50% is lawful but is not s.44ADA — it triggers s.44AA books and brings s.44AB audit into play
s.44ADA presumes a profit *from* gross receipts; a declared profit with no receipts has nothing to be a presumption of, and an earlier version discarded it silently

s.115BAC(6) read with rule 21AGA: a person without business or professional income exercises the option in the return; Form 10-IEA is for those who have it. The test is the income, never the ITR number.

s.115BAC(6) read with rule 21AGA: a person without business or professional income exercises the option in the return; Form 10-IEA is for those who have it. The test is the income, never the ITR number.

this engine has no argument for 44AD, 44AE, intraday, F&O or partner remuneration, so an empty presumptive figure is not evidence that no business income exists; asserting Form 10-IEA was unnecessary can cost the filer the old regime for the year
presumptive receipts prove business income even when nothing is declared

business income reaches this engine only through --other-slab-income, so an empty presumptive figure is not evidence of absence; a non-audit business filer's s.139(1) date is 31 August 2026 and treating unknown as no-business charges s.234F on a return that was timely

s.115BAC(6) with rule 21AGA: the test is the income, never the ITR number. forms-itr1-itr3-itr4.md records the ITR-3 A19(b)(II) path for a filer answering No to current business income, who elects in the return like anyone else

intraday is speculative business income, so the non-audit business s.139(1) date of 31 August 2026 applies and Form 10-IEA is required for the old regime — neither follows from a presumptive figure, which this filer does not have

intraday, F&O and partner remuneration are business income but not presumptive income; ITR-4 guidance belongs only to a presumptive filer, and offering it here leaves ITR-4 open to a filer the form rules send to ITR-3

[documented] s.111A applies to a short-term gain on an equity share or equity-oriented unit on which STT is paid; a short-term gain outside it is charged at the rates applicable to the total income. [documented] Schedule CG is the head-of-income schedule for a capital gain however it is taxed. [inferred] Which specific assets fall outside s.111A — a debt or gold ETF, unlisted shares held short, physical gold — follows from that section text and is not separately notified.

[observed, this engine] Routing the same figure through --other-slab-income must produce identical tax; only the head of income differs. [inferred] That equality is what makes the output usable as a Schedule CG cross-check, which is the reason the flag exists.

[documented] Capital-loss set-off and carry-forward under s.70/71/74 has an ordering, an intra-head restriction and an 8-year carry-forward requiring Schedules CYLA, BFLA and CFL. [observed, this engine] A broker reports a short-term loss as a negative figure, and it reaches slab income where the existing negative special-rate check never sees it.

[documented] ITR-4 carries no Schedule CG, so a capital gain that must be reported there cannot be filed on it whatever the presumptive position or the 50 lakh limit. [inferred] The resulting return for a presumptive filer with such a gain is ITR-3.
